AWARD 1. Vide this order I shall dispose off the claim petition filed by petitioners U/s 166 read with Section 140 of The Motor Vehicle's Act, 1988 seeking compensation from the respondents.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that on 14.09.2017 victim Sanjeet Kumar @ Sagar was going to Pant Nagar, Uttrakhant from Noida after loading goods by Maxi Truck Plus and on 15.09.2017 at about 3.00 p.m. when he reached near Hapur Dehat, NH24, PS Hapur, Dehat, Distt. Hapur, the left wheel of said Maxi Truck got punctured and he parked his vehicle at extreme left side of the road and was changing the tyre, in meanwhile a TATA 407 bearing registration no. DL1LV 0882, being driven by its driver / respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner and at a very high speed came from from back side and hit victim and said Maxi Truck with a great force.
As a result of such forceful impact, victim suffered injuries.

He was immediately taken to District Hospital, Hapur,
wherein during the treatment victim died.
His postmortem was conducted at District Mortuary Hapur, District Hapur.

3. Respondents no. 1 and 2 / driver & owner of the offending vehicle have filed their joint written statement stating that their vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case and no accident has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no. 1 and offending vehicle is not involved in the said accident.
It is further stated that their vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 and they have all valid documents of vehicle including driving licence of respondent no. 1.

However, it has taken the plea that in case it is found that there is any breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, It shall not be liable to pay any amount of compensation.
Respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has denied its liability on certain other technical grounds as well.

Respondent no. 3 /
Ins. Co. has examined respondent no. 1 as R3W1.

I have heard counsel for petitioners and counsel for respondents.

My issue wise findings are as under: ISSUE no.1 Whether Sanjeet Kumar @ Sagar (victim) died due to vehicular accident on 15.09.2017 at about 3 am Near Hapur Dehat, NH24, District Hapur due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL1LV 0882 (TATA407) by respondent no. 1 (Umesh Sharma) OPP.
8.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
To prove the same, father of deceased examined himself as PW1 and also examined eyewitness Sunil as PW2.

PW2 / eyewitness Sunil deposed that on 15.09.2017, he going to Garhmuketshwar from Noida by his car via Hapur road for holydip (gangasnan) and at about 2.30 am when he reached near Hapur Dehat, NH24, he saw a TATA 407 bearing registration no. DL1LV 0882, being driven by its driver / respondent no. 1 in a very rash and negligent manner and at a very high speed came from back side and after changing its driving lane hit driver of Maxi Truck NO. UP16ET 3288 with a great force.
As a result of forceful impact, driver of maxi truck sustained injuries.
He informed the police and ambulance reached at the spot and driver of Maxi truck was removed to the District Hospital.

In his cross examination,
PW2 Sunil denied the suggestion that he is deposing falsely or that he is not the eyewitness of accident or that he was not present at the spot or that accident occurred due to negligence on the part of victim.
No suggestion was given to PW2 Sunil with respect to the manner in which the accident had occurred.
Nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW2 Sunil.
The fact that deceased suffered fatal injuries in the accident is duly supported by his postmortem report.

There is nothing on record nor anything alleged by the respondents, particularly respondent no. 1, which Ashok Kumar - Son vs Umesh Sharma on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19876837/
5 shows that he has filed any complaint to any higher authority with respect to his false implication in the present case.

9.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and victim suffered fatal injuries in the said accident.
This issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
Whether petitioners are LRs of said victim and entitled to compensation, if yes, what amount and from whom of respondents?
OPP 10.
As far as petitioner no.2 Shyauraj Singh, father of deceased is concerned, he cannot be said to be dependent upon the deceased.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of Indian in Smt. Sarla Verma and Ors.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Civil Appeal No. 3483 of 2008 (Arising out of SLP (C) No.
8648 of 2007) decided on 15.04.2009, has held as under:  "Where the deceased was a bachelor and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma and Ors.
Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In regard to bachelors,
normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.
Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event the contribution to the parent/s and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.
Further, subject to evidence to the contrary, the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent.
In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents, because they will either be independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father.

Thus even if the deceased is survived by parents and siblings, only the mother would be considered to be a dependent, and 50% would be treated as the personal and living expenses of the bachelor and 50% as the contribution to the family."
So, only petitioner no.1, mother of deceased is considered to be entitled to compensation.
Now coming to the extent of compensation.
11. Petitioner no. 2 as PW1 has deposed that his son was 20 years of age and was working as a driver and getting salary of Rs. 16,500/.
But in his cross examination, PW2 stated that he has no documentary proof to show that his deceased son was working and earning.
Admittedly the victim was resident of UP State.
In such circumstance, earnings of deceased is to be taken to be equal to minimum wages of an unskilled labour, at the time of accident, as per UP minimum wages, which was Rs.7400.48 per month.

sentences.text: Now coming to the aspect of liability.
15. Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas and though examined respondent no. 1 as R3W1 but nothing material has come on record showing any statutory defence.
Further, no material has come on record which shows that there is any breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy of offending vehicle.

Further, the allegations levelled in the written statement howsoever strong that may be, cannot take place of proof particularly when insurance company despite having raised the issue, has not led any positive evidence on this aspect.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. holding that petitioner no. 1 is entitled to get compensation from respondent no.3 / Ins. Co.

This amount of Rs. 11,18,952.57 is allowed to petitioners as loss of dependency.
In view of the above and since the respondent no.3 / Ins. Co. has failed to establish any statutory defence, it is liable to indemnify the owner / insured and to pay compensation to the petitioner.

(a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s)
of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
(b) The original fixed deposit shall be retained by the bank in safe custody.
However, the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by bank to the claimant(s).
(e) No loan, advance, withdrawal or pre-mature discharge be allowed on the fixed deposits without permission of the Court.
(f) The concerned bank shall not issue any cheque book and/or debit card to claimant(s).
However,
in case the debit card and/or cheque book have already been issued, bank shall cancel the same before the disbursement of the award amount.
The bank shall debit card(s) freeze the account of the claimant(s) so that no debit card be issued in respect of the account of the claimant(s) from any other branch of the bank.
(g) The bank shall make an endorsement on the passbook of the claimant(s) to the effect that no cheque book and/or debit card have been issued and shall not be issued without the permission of the Court and claimant(s) shall produce the passbook with the necessary endorsement before the Ashok Kumar - Son vs Umesh Sharma on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19876837/
8 Court on the date fixed for compliance.
(h) It is clarified that the endorsement made by the bank along with the duly signed and stamped by the bank official on the passbook(s) of the claimant(s) is sufficient compliance of clause above.
Respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is directed to deposit amount of compensation, as stated above, with this tribunal within 30 days, with advance notice to petitioner.
